newsitem.title: UK: IBCA rates Russia's Mezhcombank long-term BB minus.
newsitem.headline: IBCA rates Russia's Mezhcombank long-term BB minus.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said on Monday it had assigned a long-term rating of BB minus and a short-term rating of B to Russia's Mezhcombank.
An individual of C/D and a Legal rating of 4T were also assigned to the bank, IBCA said in a statement.

"Mezhcombank (MZB) was established in June 1990 s a limited partnership and belongs to a small group of reasonably successful independent banks which have developed rapidly since then by providing efficient payments, settlements, foreign currency and asset management services to a group of core clients," IBCA said.

MIt said MZB has specialised in hard currency business including foreign exchange trading, international settlements, trade finance and hard currency loans and guarantees for large foreign trade clients.
"The bank has 76 shareholders but its eight largest accounts for around 75 percent of its equity and include several large Russian foreign trade organisations," IBCA said.
"The majority of the bank's balance sheet and its income statement is denominated in US dollars as most of its clients are exporters and earn their income in hard currency."

"The bank appears adequately reserved against its known customer and bank problem accounts. In common with other Russian banks its performance ratios have not been strong, particularly when compared with the high Russian inflation rate," IBCA said.
IBCA added that at end-1995, MZB was acceptably, but not particularly well capitalised compared with many Russian banks.
"The bank's equity has increased in 1996 through improved profitability and, consequently, higher retained earnings," it said.
The agnecy said that its Individual rating of C/D was "a reasonably strong one for a country which is not rated investment grade".
"It is likely to be one of the highest Individual ratings the agency assigns to a Russian bank which does not have foreign management of shareholders in the current environment," it said.
